about.title: Personal Injury Help in Chino Hills, California
about.longDescription: Chino Hills sits where San Bernardino County meets the Orange and Los Angeles County lines, and a lot of its traffic funnels through a handful of routes: SR-71 (the Chino Freeway), Chino Hills Parkway, Peyton Drive, and Carbon Canyon Road out toward the county line. Public records for 2025, the most recent final year, list 96 injury collisions in the city, with 131 people hurt and 2 traffic deaths. Reports tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. Those are counts, not judgments about any particular street. Behind each number, though, is someone dealing with an emergency room bill, a car that will not start, and an adjuster who keeps calling. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not give legal advice or represent anyone. What we do is connect people in Chino Hills with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases like theirs, whether it came from a crash near The Shoppes at Chino Hills, a fall at a business, or a dog bite on a neighborhood sidewalk. You pay nothing to be connected, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Chino Hills Claim

items.title: The clock is two years, sometimes less
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, you may have only six months to file a claim, so early contact matters.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your case
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. If you were found 30 percent responsible, your recovery is reduced by 30 percent, but it is not wiped out.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not put a ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, lost enjoyment of life, or emotional distress. Your claim is valued on your actual losses.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency. There is no hourly bill and no upfront retainer; the fee comes out of any recovery, and if there is none, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: Where do collisions in Chino Hills tend to show up in public records?
items.answer: Based on public-record collision counts, the corridors with the highest volume are SR-71 (the Chino Freeway), Chino Hills Parkway, Peyton Drive, and Carbon Canyon Road. In 2025 the city recorded 96 injury collisions, 131 people injured, and 2 traffic deaths. Reports tend to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These figures reflect traffic volume and reporting, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service. We match you with an independent personal injury attorney who practices in San Bernardino County, and that attorney, not LawProactive, handles your case and gives you legal advice.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a crash with a city vehicle or a fall on public property, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. Because the deadlines vary, it helps to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: What if the insurance company says the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so sharing some blame does not bar you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still pursue the remainder. An attorney can review the police report and evidence to challenge an unfair fault assignment.

items.question: What does it cost to use LawProactive and hire an attorney?
